cards.text: A long time after the LORD gave Israel rest from all their enemies, Joshua, Israel's leader, is old and well along in years. He calls in all Israel, including the elders, leaders, judges and officers. Friend, when the boss pulls EVERY department into one room, nobody is checking their phone.

cards.question: Joshua tells them they've seen everything the LORD did to these nations for their sake. He says it was the LORD their God who ___ for them.

cards.text: Joshua says he has handed out these remaining nations to the tribes as their inheritance, along with the ones he already cut off, from the Jordan west to the Great Sea, the Mediterranean. Giving out land with people still living on it? That takes CONFIDENCE.

cards.question: About the nations still in the land, Joshua says the LORD their God will ___ them out, so Israel can ___ their land.

cards.text: Now Joshua gets to his charge, and he tells them to be very strong. That's personal-trainer-at-six-in-the-morning energy, friend, and at six in the morning I can barely get my apron tied.

cards.question: Joshua tells Israel to be very strong. Strong enough to do what?

answers.text: Keep all that's written in the Law of Moses
Drive out every nation all by themselves
Build a great temple for the LORD

cards.question: Joshua says it's okay for Israel to turn aside from the Book of the Law a little, as long as they keep most of it.

cards.text: Now about those nations still living among them, Joshua says not to associate with them. No hanging out, no group chat, NOTHING.

cards.question: Joshua tells Israel they must not swear by the gods of those nations.
Instead of the gods of those nations, who does Joshua tell Israel to hold fast to, as they've done to this day?

cards.text: Joshua points back at the record: the LORD has driven out great and powerful nations before Israel, and to this day no one can stand against them. Me, I once lost an argument to the dead batteries I shared that drawer with, and they had NO charge.

cards.question: Because the LORD fights for them, just as He promised, Joshua says one Israelite can put a crowd of enemies to flight. How big a crowd?
So Joshua tells Israel to watch themselves carefully. What does he want them watching for?

answers.text: That they love the LORD their God
That their borders stay well guarded
That their armies stay ready to fight

cards.text: Then Joshua flips it around: what if they turn away, cling to the nations still among them, and intermarry and associate with them? Friend, this is where the meeting goes from "great job, team" to "okay, listen UP."

cards.question: Joshua says that if Israel clings to those nations, the LORD will keep driving those nations out anyway.
Joshua warns that if Israel clings to those nations, those nations will become something for Israel. What will they become?

answers.text: Something that traps and hurts them

cards.text: Then Joshua says, "Now behold, today I am going the way of all the earth," and he reminds them of something they know with all their heart and soul.

cards.question: Joshua says some of the good promises the LORD made to Israel have failed along the way.
Joshua says that just as every good thing the LORD promised came to pass, the LORD will also bring the calamity He threatened.
Joshua says the anger of the LORD would burn against Israel. What would bring that on?

answers.text: Breaking His covenant and serving other gods
Losing a battle to the nations around them
Leaving the land to go live somewhere else

cards.text: Go that way, Joshua says, and they will quickly perish from this good land the LORD gave them. I think that's an old man who means every single word.
